correctness.rationale: For O=K6 minus 01,23,45 the exact face vector is (12,30,8). Every pair of disjoint graph edges lies in at most one perfect matching (unique two unused vertices), so all eight triangles have free 1-faces; eight elementary simplicial collapses leave a connected graph with 12 vertices and 22 edges, hence M(O) is a wedge of 11 circles with torsion-free integral homology. The octahedral group is C2 wreath S3 = S4 times C2. Since only H0 and H1 occur, signed fixed-simplex Euler traces give the H1 character. The executable constructs all 48 group elements and independently transports 11 explicit integral fundamental cycles across all 48 actions, verifies 2304 exact integral composition laws, and compares all traces to Euler–Poincare; ten S4 times C2 character inner products equal the listed multiplicities and sum to dimension 11. The group action and sign normalization are fixed by signed permutations of the three antipodal coordinate pairs. No infinite-family extrapolation or external audit is claimed.

originality.rationale: Primary-text comparisons distinguish the ordinary matching complex on twelve edge-vertices from a separately published Morse complex on twenty-four incidence-vertices; neither the 2022 matching-complex computations for paths, cycles and windmills nor the complete-hypergraph representation theorem contains the eleven-dimensional rational octahedral character. The equivariant graph matching-number theorem concerns graded permutation modules, not homology. Searches by octahedral graph, cocktail-party graph, K6 minus a perfect matching, Weyl B3, rotation group S4, and inversion trace did not locate an equivalent published result. This is a bounded literature conclusion rather than absolute proof of novelty.
residual_risks: The search and source inspections do not exclude a differently indexed or unpublished octahedral matching-homology calculation.

value.rationale: The regular octahedron is the canonical 3-dimensional cross-polytope with a full rank-three reflection group. Identifying all four nontrivial rational irreducible constituents and distinguishing central inversion parity (3 even and 8 odd dimensions) is information invisible in the 11-circle homotopy type and not forced by the complete-graph case. The exact finite group representation, including vanishing full-group invariants, supplies a natural base example for equivariant topology of cocktail-party matching complexes. The result does not depend on an arbitrary graph slice or claim significance merely because the checker works; it resolves the entire symmetry character for this canonical object.
